title: Eval cascade kickoff on version locks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: When customers or catalog owners lock (pin) model versions or change serving configs, we currently rely on ad-hoc eval runs and manual monitoring to detect quality regressions. That creates blind spots, delayed rollbacks, and inconsistent coverage across tenants.

Goal: Implement an automated 'eval cascade' that kicks off a prioritized sequence of lightweight to heavyweight evaluations whenever a version lock or catalog upgrade occurs. The cascade should be tenant-aware, cost-budgeted, and fast enough to provide actionable signals for canary promotion/rollback.

Scope: Catalog model pins and customer tenant pins for hosted/dedicated/private. The feature will cover: (1) trigger rules and sampling policy, (2) priority fanout across tenant tiers, (3) lightweight smoke + few-shot fidelity checks, (4) deeper fidelity suites when initial checks flag regressions, (5) automatic alerting and optional auto-rollback hooks for critical regressions.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement full eval authoring UI or long-term storage/analysis of eval artifacts (will integrate with metrics pipeline later). It also excludes eval-driven billing adjustments (separate work).
acceptance_criteria: A trigger is emitted for every catalog or tenant version lock event and recorded in the eval-orchestrator queue.
Sampling policy supports: full-run, tenant-sampled (percentage), and sticky-sample per tenant for a configurable window.
Cascade stages: smoke (latency + token-level checks), fidelity-light (subset of evaluation dataset), fidelity-deep (full prioritized probes) implementable and configurable per project.
Priority and throttling: higher-tier customers can be prioritized, and global budget caps prevent runaway costs.
When the cascade flags a regression above threshold, the system posts to the configured webhook, creates an incident draft, and optionally triggers a rollback policy if enabled by tenant.
Telemetry: per-trigger metrics appear on the console with counts, avg eval time, cost estimate, and pass/fail rates within the release window.
End-to-end E2 trigger + smoke stage completes within target SLO of 3 minutes for sample tenants under normal load.
milestones: Design policy spec and sampling matrix (week 1)
API contract for trigger events + tenant overrides (week 2)
Pilot with internal catalog and 5 beta tenants (week 5)
notes: Trade-offs considered: running full evals for all pin events gives best signal but costs too much. We favor a multi-stage cascade to balance signal and cost.
Sticky sampling idea: once a tenant is sampled as part of a pin event, keep sampling the tenant for 24-72 hours to detect delayed regressions for that tenant's traffic profile.
Failure modes: eval infra outage should not block model promotion; fallback is to mark as 'eval skipped' and surface to on-call and product owner.
Cost guard: default per-pin budget is 10 compute-minutes; admins can override per-tenant. Exceeding budget pauses deeper stages and posts a cost alert.
